title: Girlfriend says man shot by police officer 'gentle, kind'
article: The 18-year-old Burnaby man shot by Port Moody Police Monday had a big heart and a gentle soul, according to his girlfriend of six months.
The 16-year-old girl, who only identified herself as Sami, told The NOW that shooting victim Keyvan Tabesh was "gentle, kind and always giving."

Tabesh was shot by a plainclothes Port Moody police officer in a cul-de-sac around 2 a.m. Monday, July 14. Police said Tabesh and two friends had pulled into the dead-end road, and the exit had been blocked by the officer's unmarked car.

Police said Tabesh and at least one of the other men got out the car. Tabesh allegedly rushed the officer with a raised machete and was shot and killed. A second man was shot and remains in hospital. In all, five shots were fired by the officer.
"He shot him in the heart and he had such a good heart," said an emotional Sami from Tabesh's mother's home in Burnaby. "Why would they shoot him in the heart?"

The officer was responding to a call put out by on-duty police, who had received a complaint from two women that a man driving a car matching the description of Tabesh's vehicle bumped their car, and a man with a machete threatened them and broke a window.
She said it was out of character for her boyfriend to behave the way described in police and media reports this week.

Police have said they believe the officer, who was in the area on an unrelated matter, identified himself as a police officer, although they continue to investigate and interview witnesses at the scene.
Sami said she had been with Tabesh most of the day and noticed his demeanor change that evening.

"When he came to pick me up earlier that day, he had a big smile. But later on, he wasn't himself. I kept asking him what was wrong. He said he didn't know what was wrong. He said something in his mind was bothering him," Sami said.
She said Tabesh admitted he was missing a close friend who had recently returned to Iran. She said he called his father to see if he could get news about the friend.
"He started crying on the phone," she said.
She said she doesn't know what happened after that.
"We were at his house with his friends. He dropped me off and went out. I didn't know what happened until I went to his house the next day," she said.
She said Tabesh was driving his brother's car the night of the shooting. Inside the car was a machete his brother had bought for camping.
"He just had it in the car," Sami said.
However, she said Tabesh, a bodybuilder, did feel he had to protect himself after arriving in Canada from Iran two years ago.

She said people wanted to fight him because they were "jealous" of him. She said in one such encounter, Tabesh was challenged by another man and when they began to fight, the other man pulled out some sort of weapon and slashed Tabesh's face. He needed over a dozen stitches to close the wound.
After that incident, she said, Tabesh began to carry a pocket knife.
"Since that day he felt they (fights) weren't fair, so he felt he had to protect himself."
She said he was not a violent person. "He never laid a hand on people," she said.
In fact, she said, he was kind, gentle and loved by all those who knew him.
"He was always doing everything for people, always helping his friends and family," Sami said. "Even if someone did something bad to him, he would always be there for them."
She said two acts of kindness stick out for her.
The last one was Canada Day.
"He saw a poor man and he parked his car and ran over and put some change down and came back," she said.
Another time, they saw a man who looked down on his luck. She said Tabesh stopped and gave the man a ride -- "He said he felt better," after he helped someone.
Sami said they talked about getting married and they were going to celebrate her 17th birthday together on July 31.
Tabesh's funeral was Friday.
The unidentified 25-year police veteran has taken a leave and is receiving trauma counselling.
Const. Brian Soles, Port Moody Police spokesperson, said before the incident Monday the officer had never fired his weapon in the line of duty.
An autopsy was completed this week.
